text:
The act of State doctrine means a domestic court will not judge the legality of a recognized foreign sovereign’s public acts done inside that sovereign’s own territory, and will treat those acts as valid. It is a rule of judicial abstention, separate from State immunity, so it neither makes every State act immune nor treats courts as well placed to decide whether the State committed a tort. Challenges belong to diplomacy or that foreign State’s own legal system, subject to narrow modern limits such as territorial scope and fundamental public policy.
